newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Cathay's Tsai is Taiwan's richest person.
newsitem.headline: Cathay's Tsai is Taiwan's richest person.

text.p: Cathay Life Insurance chairman Tsai Wan-lin is Taiwan's richest person with a fortune of T$275 billion (US$10 billion), the April edition of Taiwan's Excellency magazine reported on Friday.
In 1996, Forbes magazine listed Tsai as the world's fifth-richest man with personal assets worth US$12.2 billion.
A ranking released by Excellency rated Wu Tung-chin, head of the Shin Kong Life Insurance, as the country's second-richest person with assets worth T$105 billion.
Douglas Hsu of Far East group ranked third with T$75 billion, the magazine said.
Hsu was followed by petrochemical giant Formosa Plastic chairman Wang Yung-ching, who owns T$65 billion, and his brother Wang Yung-tsai with T$60 billion.
Shipping magnate Chang Yung-fa of Evergreen Marine group was sixth with T$55 billion, followed by Tsai Wan-tsai's T$53 billion and Koo Chen-fu's T$32 billion.
Tsai Wan-tsai is a brother of Tsai Wan-lin. Koo, who is Taiwan's top negotiator with rival China, heads the giant conglomerate Koo's Group.

Koo is head of the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation that handles dialogues with China in the absence of formal ties. Taiwan has banned official contacts with China since they split at the end of a civil war in 1949.
